facts.text: On this date in 1957, the Soviet Union launched Sputnik 2 — carrying Laika the dog into orbit with no plan to bring her back. She became the first living creature in space, and died within hours from overheating.
On this date in 1903, Panama declared independence from Colombia — with the US Navy blocking Colombian ships from intervening. The canal treaty was signed just two weeks later.

Mongolia has more horses than people. With 3.5 million residents and roughly 4.3 million horses, it holds the world's highest horse-to-human ratio, and nearly a third of its population still lives nomadically.
The city of Chongqing, China is home to over 32 million people — larger than Australia's entire population — yet most Westerners have never heard of it.
More people live inside a 40-mile radius of Jakarta than in the entire country of Canada.
On Nov 3, 1979, the Dow closed at 800. It would take just 8 more years to hit 2,000 — then only 2 more years to hit 3,000. Markets compress time in ways humans never expect.
On Nov 3, 1992, while America voted for Clinton, the S&P 500 rose 0.4%. Markets had already priced in his win — election days rarely move stocks because traders vote early with money.
The New York Stock Exchange was founded in 1792 under a buttonwood tree by 24 brokers. The tree is gone. The commissions remain.
Saudi Aramco's 2019 IPO raised $25.6 billion — the largest in history. It valued the company at $1.7 trillion, briefly making it worth more than Apple, Google, and Amazon combined.
The entire global bond market — roughly $130 trillion — is larger than world GDP. Most of it trades with no central exchange, no ticker, and no price that ordinary investors ever see.
On this date in 1957, Sputnik 2 carried Laika into orbit — the first living creature to circle Earth. She proved spaceflight was survivable. Scientists knew she wouldn't return.
Your skeleton is not static. Every bone in your body is fully replaced, cell by cell, approximately every decade.
On November 3, 1994, the first confirmed pulsar in a binary system earned its discoverers a Nobel Prize retroactively confirmed. Pulsars spin up to 716 times per second.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
The human eye can detect a single photon in total darkness. Your brain suppresses this sensitivity during daylight so the world doesn't look like static.
On this day in 1957, the Soviet Union launched Laika into orbit — making a dog an astronaut before any human had left the atmosphere.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. Medieval Europe had tenure before Tenochtitlan had walls.
On this day in 1783, the Continental Army disbanded — soldiers walked home carrying muskets, with no pensions, no ceremony, no state to thank them.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She was ancient history to ancient Egyptians.
The fax machine was patented in 1843 — 33 years before the telephone. You could transmit a document before you could transmit a voice.

Mamihlapinatapai (Yaghan): the look shared between two people who both want something but neither will initiate. One of the world's most succinct words, from a language with only a handful of living speakers.

Sonder (English, coined 2012): the realization that every passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. John Koenig invented it for his Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, and it spread as if it had always existed.
On this date in 1957, Sputnik 2 launched, carrying Laika into orbit. The Russian word sputnik simply means 'fellow traveler' — a satellite, literally, is just something that travels alongside.
Forelsket (Norwegian): the euphoric, almost painful feeling of falling in love. English has no single word for it, which says something about what English chose to name and what it let slip past.
Acedia (Greek/Latin): spiritual torpor, a numb inability to care. Medieval monks considered it the deadliest of sins — not wickedness, but the slow failure to find anything worth feeling.
On this date in 2008, Satoshi Nakamoto published the Bitcoin whitepaper to a cryptography mailing list. Nine people responded. None predicted it would anchor a $1T asset class.
On Nov 3, 2021, Solana suffered its first major network outage — 17 hours offline after a bot flood during an IDO minted 400,000 transactions per second, overwhelming validators.
Bitcoin's genesis block contains the headline 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks.' Satoshi embedded it permanently — part timestamp proof, part indictment.
Ethereum's EIP-1559 destroyed over 4.7 million ETH since August 2021. The burn mechanism turned transaction fees from miner revenue into a deflationary force built into base protocol.
The most expensive NFT ever settled on-chain was Beeple's 'Everydays' at $69M — but the buyer, Metakovan, paid in WETH wrapped inside a smart contract, never touching fiat.
On this date in 2017, Google Brain published 'Attention Is All You Need,' introducing the Transformer architecture that now underlies virtually every large language model in production.
On November 3, 2022, Meta released OPT-IML, one of the first large instruction-tuned models released with full weights — a quiet opening move in the open-weights era.
AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins before most structural biology labs had processed a dozen — compressing decades of potential work into roughly 18 months of inference.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed around 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of about 4,500 average US households.
The first neural network to defeat a professional Go player, AlphaGo, used a policy network trained on 30 million moves from human games before it learned to surpass those humans entirely.
